>> MUSIC
Children gain a firm understanding of music through listening, singing, playing, evaluating, analysing, and composing across a wide variety of historical periods, styles and traditions.
Discrete lessons enable children to engage with a broad range of musical genres and forms, whilst also proving the outlet in which they will become familiar with different instruments. Music lessons are designed to be both practical and theoretical, supporting growth in skills and a more rounded understanding of Music.

>> ART
Our Art curriculum is designed to engage, inspire and challenge pupils, equipping them with the knowledge and skills to experiment, invent and create their own works of art, craft and design.
Our sequenced curriculum enables pupils to progress and to think critically and develop a more rigorous understanding of art and design. All pupils will develop skills through drawing, painting and sculpture and learn about great artists, craft makers and designers, and understand the historical and cultural development of their art forms.

>> GEOGRAPHY
Our Geography curriculum is designed to develop children’s curiosity and fascination about the world and its people that will remain with them for the rest of their lives.
Children are encouraged to develop a greater understanding and knowledge of the world, as well as their place in it. Geography is, by nature, an investigative subject, which develops an understanding of concepts, knowledge and skills. The sequenced curriculum is designed to ensure that pupils develop contextual knowledge of the location of globally significant places including their defining physical and human characteristics and how these provide a geographical context for understanding the actions of processes.

>> HISTORY
It is our aim to instil a love of History in all our children. The study of history ignites children’s curiosity about the past in Britain and the wider world.
Through finding out about how and why the world, our country, cultures and local communities have developed over time, children understand how the past influences the present. What they learn through history can influence their decisions about personal choices, attitudes and values. Our sequenced curriculum will develop knowledge, skills and understanding by ensuring that pupils gain historical perspective by placing their growing knowledge into different contexts, understanding the connections between local, regional, national and international history; between cultural, economic, military, political, religious and social history; and between short- and long-term timescales.

>> MATHS
By delivering a planned and sequenced mathematics curriculum, we aim to equip our children with efficiency and depth of understanding that allows them to use and apply their mathematical knowledge and skills. This will ensure our children are confident mathematicians and develop a love and excitement for the subject that will carry them through into the next stages of their education and beyond.
We aim to increase pupil confidence in maths so they are able to express themselves and their ideas using the language of maths with assurance.
The teaching of mathematics provides opportunities for group work, paired work and whole class teaching enabling pupils to engage in:
Explanation and reasoning
The development of mental strategies
Written methods
Practical work
Investigational work
Problem- solving
Mathematical discussion
Consolidation of basic skills and routines.

>> PSHE
Our PSHE programme promotes children’s personal, social and economic development, as well as their health and wellbeing. It helps to give children the knowledge, skills and understanding they need to lead confident, healthy, independent lives and to become informed, active, responsible citizens.
Pupils are supported to be active learners who can express themselves and accept difference in their community and the wider world. Celebration of difference as well as personal achievements, promotes a culture of equality in our school. Promoting citizenship through PSHE enables children to make a positive contribution by developing the knowledge and experience needed to claim their rights and understand their responsibilities.

>> RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
The intent of our R.E curriculum is to nurture and develop their individual knowledge and understanding of the rich diverse community they live in. This is through systematic enquiry into religion and world views and providing a space to allow thought provoking challenging questions about meaning and purpose in life.
The children can develop their understanding and skills needed to appreciate and value varied responses to these questions and develop responses of their own. This promotes our children’s sense of personal identity, fostering deeper meaning behind ideas, values and purpose in the local, national and wider global community.

>> SCIENCE
The curriculum is designed to equip pupils with the skills to work scientifically, asking and answering their own questions through using a range of different enquiry types. Children will learn to be scientifically literate and have a strong understanding of scientific vocabulary in the curriculum.

>> SEND
At Kingfisher Primary School, we seek to provide an education where all children are valued, included and enabled to achieve their potential to function, learn and succeed by providing appropriate support to meet their needs.
We believe that all children including those with special educational needs and/or disability (SEND) should have their needs met, normally in mainstream school and be offered full access to a broad, balanced and relevant curriculum.
We aim to do this by closely following the DfES Code of Practice on the Identification and Assessment of Educational Needs. The school also gives regard to the guidance specified in the Special Educational Needs Disability Discrimination Act 2005 and the Lamb Inquiry 2009.
Kingfisher’s Special Educational Needs and/or Disabilities Coordinator (SENDco) is Hannah Lawrence. You can contact Hannah via the school office.

>> DESIGN TECHNOLOGY
Design and Technology is an inspiring, rigorous and practical subject. Using creativity and imagination, pupils design and make products that solve real and relevant problems within a variety of contexts, considering their own and others’ needs, wants and values.
Children acquire a broad range of subject knowledge and draw on knowledge and understanding gained in mathematics, science, engineering, computing and art and learn how to become innovative, enterprising, resourceful and confident. Our sequenced curriculum ensures that pupils develop the creative, technical and practical expertise needed to perform everyday tasks
